---
title: "Learning Robot Learning"
subtitle: "Concepts, pictures, and code for ETH Zürich's *Robot Learning* course"
---

This site is an independent, unofficial companion to ETH Zürich's *Robot Learning: From Fundamentals to Foundation Models*, taught by Oier Mees in Spring 2026. The [course page]({{< var course_url >}}) has the lecture recordings, slides, and homework.

Each course week has a page with the big picture, intuitions, the key equations explained term by term, worked NumPy examples, interactive figures, a short animation of the week's key idea, a PyTorch sketch of the core algorithm, and summaries of the papers and the guest talk.

## The course in one picture

The course moves from the robot itself to the models that are starting to control it (@fig-course-arc). The first weeks set up the robot and the language for its decisions, then the two ways a robot can learn behaviour: by copying demonstrations and by trial and error. The middle of the course is the architectures of the foundation-model era: generative models, transformers and world models. The last weeks put them together into generalist, reasoning policies, and ask what is still missing.

## Weeks

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Foundations

| Week | The question it answers |
|---|---|
| [1 · Introduction to Robot Learning](weeks/w01-introduction.qmd) | Why can't we simply program robots for our homes, and what does learning from data change? |
| [2 · Robot Control & MDPs](weeks/w02-robot-control-mdps.qmd) | How does a goal become motor commands, and how do we describe the decisions above that? |

## Learning behaviour

| Week | The question it answers |
|---|---|
| [3 · Imitation Learning](weeks/w03-imitation-learning.qmd) | How do demonstrations become a policy, and why does copying break down? |
| [4 · Reinforcement Learning I](weeks/w04-reinforcement-learning-1.qmd) | How can a robot learn from rewards alone, with and without a model? (values, Q-learning, DQN) |
| [5 · Reinforcement Learning II](weeks/w05-reinforcement-learning-2.qmd) | How do you follow the gradient of reward through a world you can't differentiate? (policy gradients, PPO, SAC) |

## Modern architectures

| Week | The question it answers |
|---|---|
| [6 · Generative Models](weeks/w06-generative-models.qmd) | How can a policy represent a complicated distribution over actions? (diffusion, flow matching) |
| [7 · Sequence Modeling and Transformers](weeks/w07-sequence-modeling-transformers.qmd) | How do observations, words and actions become one sequence a transformer learns from? |
| [8 · World Models](weeks/w08-world-models.qmd) | How do you learn what your actions will do, and use it? |

## Putting it together

| Week | The question it answers |
|---|---|
| [9 · Generalist Robot Policies](weeks/w09-generalist-robot-policies.qmd) | How do you train one policy for many robots, and tell whether it works? |
| [10 · Embodied Reasoning and Test-time Scaling](weeks/w10-embodied-reasoning.qmd) | Can a robot that thinks harder act better, and when is thinking worth its cost? |

## Looking ahead

| Week | The question it answers |
|---|---|
| [11 · Frontiers & Open Problems](weeks/w11-frontiers.qmd) | What is still unsolved, and which ideas point towards solutions? |
| [12 · Guest Lectures](weeks/w12-guest-lectures.qmd) | How do the pieces fit together? (the course reviewed in one table; the guest talk is not available online) |

:::

## How to use this site

Each week's page is laid out the same way:

1. **Big picture:** where the week fits, its key ideas and its vocabulary.
2. **Intuition:** a concrete story and pictures before any math, with ▶ links to the moment in the lecture video where each idea is taught.
3. **Key concepts & formulae:** the equations, in the course's notation, each explained in words and term by term.
4. **Worked examples:** the ideas applied to real numbers.
5. **Interactive:** figures you can change.
6. **Algorithm & code:** the NumPy code that produced the page's figures, beside a PyTorch sketch of how you would write it at scale.
7. **Papers** and **Guest spotlight:** original summaries of the papers discussed in class and of the guest talk.
8. **Solved problems**, **Recap** and **Cheat sheet:** try each problem before opening its solution.

Big picture and Intuition are written to stand alone: reading just those two sections of every week gives a tour of the whole course. Week 12 is shorter, since it has no lecture.

The pages never reproduce the course's slides or homework solutions; the [course page]({{< var course_url >}}) is the place for those.

Three reference pages collect material from across the site:

- [Papers](papers.qmd): every paper card, grouped by week.
- [Glossary](glossary.qmd): every symbol and term, grouped by week, with a table of symbols that change meaning.
- [Cheat sheets](cheatsheets.qmd): every week's key equations in one place.

For the decision-making theory underneath Weeks 2 to 5, the sibling [ADM Companion]({{< var adm_url >}}/) goes deeper.
